title: Continuous delivery and continuous deployment: the difference

videos.script: A green build is a verdict on the code. Nobody can use it yet. This lesson takes shipquote the rest of the way, from a passing commit to a program answering in an environment. {{verdict}} First the words. Continuous delivery means any green commit could go to production at any moment, and a person chooses when. Continuous deployment means it goes on its own. {{words}} Then the artifact. One tarball, built once from a tag, named by its hash. You will build it twice and get the same hash both times. {{artifact}} Then the deploy, as one command. It checks the hash, unpacks the release beside the others, switches a link and runs a smoke test. {{deploy}} You will watch the smoke test stop a deploy with a typo in its configuration. And you will watch the hash check refuse an artifact that changed by one byte. {{refusals}} The lesson ends with the part of a release that is hardest to change. The database, which old and new code share while a deploy happens. {{database}}
